results.evidence: Direct evidence from the working tree. _parse_budget now returns format(amount, 'f'), and it also rejects exponent input with 'plain digits' (that rejection is carried over from CCGE-035). The docstring states the stored format: plain fixed-point digits, never scientific notation. The new tests/test_inbound_budget_format.py parametrizes '1e3', '1E3', '2.5e4' and '1e-3' and expects InquiryError. It also checks that fixed-point text is stored unchanged, including '0.0000001' (the case where str(Decimal) gives '1E-7'). uv run --offline pytest: 938 passed. ruff check, mypy and ruff format --check all pass. I did not mutation-test the 'f' change. The explicit rejection of 'e' input means the 'f' format is only exercised by the small-value test '0.0000001'.
